"""Semiautomaton-simulation scaffold for MLS-Bench — parallel-time edition.

Research question: which **parallel-time architecture** (and AdamW recipe)
best LEARNS to simulate hard finite-state semiautomata from full state
supervision, within a fixed online-training budget?

Setup follows Liu, Ash, Goel, Krishnamurthy & Zhang, "Transformers Learn
Shortcuts to Automata" (ICLR 2023, arXiv:2210.10749): sequences of length
T = 100, online training with a freshly drawn batch at every step, batch
size 16, AdamW, per-position cross-entropy on the full state sequence
(App. B.1.1 / B.3). Their headline finding: shallow non-recurrent networks
learn o(T)-depth "shortcuts" to solvable semiautomata, but accuracy on the
non-solvable S5 word problem climbs slowly with depth (Fig. 3a, best of 20
replicates: depth-1 7.9%, depth-8 51.8%, depth-9 97.2%, depth-16 99.9%).
Simulating a non-solvable group is NC1-complete (Barrington, JCSS 1989),
so no constant-depth parallel model can express it (unless TC0 = NC1), and
Merrill, Petty & Sabharwal, "The Illusion of State in State-Space Models"
(ICML 2024, arXiv:2404.08819) prove diagonal linear recurrences (S4/Mamba
family) sit in L-uniform TC0 — they need depth growing with T on exactly
this problem.

IMPORTANT — why recurrent models are excluded here: NC1-hardness only
constrains models whose serial computation depth does not grow with T.
A sequential RNN simulates ANY finite automaton by construction; both
reference papers use it as the trivial skyline (Liu et al. Fig. 5: a
1-layer LSTM reaches 100% on every task; Merrill et al. Fig. 3: a 1-layer
RNN solves every word problem). The open research question lives entirely
in the parallel-time regime, so this scaffold enforces it structurally
with two FIXED runtime guards that are *measured*, never self-reported:

  1. a module scan rejecting `nn.LSTM / nn.GRU / nn.RNN / *Cell` instances;
  2. an autograd-graph serial-depth probe: the longest path in the backward
     graph at seq_len 1024 may exceed the one at seq_len 256 by at most 80
     nodes. Per-token (or fine-grained chunkwise) python recurrences fail;
     attention, convolutions, and log-depth associative scans pass.

The transition tables are driver-private (`_PRIVATE_TABLES`) and the
automaton seed is masked before editable code sees the config: the model
must LEARN the automaton from sampled (input, state) streams. Hard-coding
or reconstructing any transition table inside the editable block is out of
contract, and an init-time tripwire aborts any run whose *untrained* model
already beats 25% accuracy (chance is at most 1/24).

The editable region exposes three functions:
  1. `build_model(env_spec, config)` returns an `nn.Module` mapping a token
     id sequence `[B, T]` to per-position state logits `[B, T, Q]`.
  2. `get_optimizer_config(config)` returns AdamW hyperparameters.
  3. `forward_logits(model, input_ids, env_spec)` is the inference wrapper.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import itertools
import json
import math
import random
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, replace
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable

import torch
from torch import nn
import torch.nn.functional as F


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: Benchmark configuration
# =====================================================================
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EnvSpec:
    """Public environment description. Transition tables are driver-private."""

    name: str
    alphabet_size: int
    num_states: int
    seq_len: int   # training/eval sequence length (Liu et al. 2023: T = 100)
    max_len: int   # maximum length the model must support (depth probe uses it)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TaskConfig:
    env_name: str = "s5_word"
    seq_len: int = 100            # Liu et al. 2023 App. B.1.1: T = 100
    train_steps: int = 40_000
    batch_size: int = 16          # Liu et al. 2023 App. B.3 (GPT-2 recipe)
    eval_batches: int = 48
    log_interval: int = 1000
    seed: int = 0
    max_grad_norm: float = 1.0
    dfa_seed: int = 1234          # unused by the group word problems; masked (-1)
    early_stop_acc: float = 0.999
    early_stop_windows: int = 3
    # parallel-time guard
    depth_probe_short: int = 256
    depth_probe_long: int = 1024
    depth_slack: int = 80
    init_tripwire_acc: float = 0.25


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class OptimizerConfig:
    lr: float
    wd: float
    beta1: float
    beta2: float


def set_global_seed(seed: int) -> None:
    random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)


def sinusoidal_table(max_len: int, d_model: int) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Fixed sinusoidal positional encodings (Vaswani et al. 2017).

    Liu et al. 2023 report their main results with sinusoidal encodings
    (App. B.1.1); shared here so every architecture can reuse it.
    """
    position = torch.arange(max_len, dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(1)
    div = torch.exp(
        torch.arange(0, d_model, 2, dtype=torch.float32)
        * (-math.log(10000.0) / d_model)
    )
    table = torch.zeros(max_len, d_model)
    table[:, 0::2] = torch.sin(position * div)
    table[:, 1::2] = torch.cos(position * div[: d_model // 2])
    return table


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: Environments
# =====================================================================
# Driver-private transition tables, keyed by env name. Reading, copying, or
# reconstructing these from the editable block is OUT OF CONTRACT: the model
# must learn the automaton from the sampled (input, state) streams alone.
_PRIVATE_TABLES: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}


# Liu et al. 2023, App. B.1.1: "The generator set for S_n consists of the
# minimal generators, a transposition and an n-cycle, as well as 6 other
# permutations ... chosen following the ordering given by the
# sympy.combinatorics package". The "6 other" are the first six
# elements of `SymmetricGroup(n).generate()` (sympy 1.14) that are neither the
# identity nor one of the two minimal generators, frozen here so the image
# needs no sympy. Permutations are array forms: p[i] is the image of i.
_GROUP_ALPHABETS: dict[str, list[tuple[int, ...]]] = {
    "s4_word": [(1, 0, 2, 3), (1, 2, 3, 0),            # (1 2), (1 2 3 4)
                (2, 3, 0, 1), (3, 1, 2, 0), (0, 2, 3, 1),
                (1, 3, 0, 2), (2, 0, 1, 3), (3, 2, 0, 1)],
    "s5_word": [(1, 0, 2, 3, 4), (1, 2, 3, 4, 0),      # (1 2), (1 2 3 4 5)
                (0, 1, 4, 2, 3), (1, 2, 0, 3, 4), (2, 3, 1, 4, 0),
                (3, 4, 2, 0, 1), (4, 1, 0, 2, 3), (0, 2, 3, 1, 4)],
}


def _group_word(config: TaskConfig) -> tuple[EnvSpec, torch.Tensor]:
    """A symmetric-group word problem of Liu et al. 2023 (App. B.1.1).

    States are the elements of the group the letters generate (all n! permutations
    for these generator sets), sorted lexicographically, identity first (state 0).
    The state is the running left-product g_t = a_t o g_{t-1} from the identity,
    and each letter a_t is drawn uniformly from the paper's generator set. S4 is
    solvable (constant-depth shortcuts exist, Liu et al. Thm. 2); S5 is not: its
    word problem is NC1-complete (Barrington 1989) and Merrill et al. 2024 prove
    it inexpressible by diagonal SSMs.
    """
    name = config.env_name
    alphabet = _GROUP_ALPHABETS[name]
    n = len(alphabet[0])

    def compose(p: tuple[int, ...], q: tuple[int, ...]) -> tuple[int, ...]:
        # (p o q)(i) = p[q[i]] -- apply q first, then p.
        return tuple(p[q[i]] for i in range(n))

    # the group the letters generate (all of S_n, A_n, ...), sorted, identity first
    identity = tuple(range(n))
    seen, frontier = {identity}, [identity]
    while frontier:
        nxt = []
        for g in frontier:
            for a in alphabet:
                h = compose(a, g)
                if h not in seen:
                    seen.add(h)
                    nxt.append(h)
        frontier = nxt
    elements = sorted(seen)
    index = {p: i for i, p in enumerate(elements)}

    Q, Sigma = len(elements), len(alphabet)
    delta = torch.zeros(Q, Sigma, dtype=torch.long)
    for qi, elem in enumerate(elements):
        for ai, a in enumerate(alphabet):
            delta[qi, ai] = index[compose(a, elem)]
    spec = EnvSpec(
        name=name,
        alphabet_size=Sigma,
        num_states=Q,
        seq_len=config.seq_len,
        max_len=max(config.seq_len, config.depth_probe_long),
    )
    return spec, delta


_ENV_BUILDERS: dict[str, Callable[[TaskConfig], tuple[EnvSpec, torch.Tensor]]] = {
    "s4_word": _group_word,
    "s5_word": _group_word,
}


def build_env_spec(config: TaskConfig) -> EnvSpec:
    if config.env_name not in _ENV_BUILDERS:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown env {config.env_name!r}")
    spec, delta = _ENV_BUILDERS[config.env_name](config)
    _PRIVATE_TABLES[spec.name] = delta
    return spec


def sample_batch(spec: EnvSpec, batch_size: int, length: int,
                 generator: torch.Generator) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Walk the (private) transition table from state 0 for `length` steps."""
    delta = _PRIVATE_TABLES[spec.name]
    inputs = torch.randint(
        0, spec.alphabet_size, (batch_size, length),
        generator=generator, dtype=torch.long,
    )
    cur = torch.zeros(batch_size, dtype=torch.long)
    states = torch.zeros(batch_size, length, dtype=torch.long)
    for t in range(length):
        cur = delta[cur, inputs[:, t]]
        states[:, t] = cur
    return inputs, states


def normalize_optimizer_config(cfg: dict[str, float]) -> OptimizerConfig:
    required = {"lr", "wd", "beta1", "beta2"}
    missing = required - set(cfg)
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"Missing optimizer hyperparameters: {sorted(missing)}")
    out = OptimizerConfig(
        lr=float(cfg["lr"]),
        wd=float(cfg["wd"]),
        beta1=float(cfg["beta1"]),
        beta2=float(cfg["beta2"]),
    )
    if out.lr <= 0:
        raise ValueError("AdamW learning rate must be positive.")
    if out.wd < 0:
        raise ValueError("AdamW weight decay must be non-negative.")
    if not 0.0 < out.beta1 < 1.0:
        raise ValueError("AdamW beta1 must satisfy 0 < beta1 < 1.")
    if not 0.0 < out.beta2 < 1.0:
        raise ValueError("AdamW beta2 must satisfy 0 < beta2 < 1.")
    return out


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: parallel-time guards (measured, never self-reported)
# =====================================================================
_FORBIDDEN_RECURRENT = (nn.LSTM, nn.GRU, nn.RNN, nn.RNNBase,
                        nn.LSTMCell, nn.GRUCell, nn.RNNCell)


def check_no_recurrent_modules(model: nn.Module) -> None:
    for mod in model.modules():
        if isinstance(mod, _FORBIDDEN_RECURRENT):
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Recurrent module {type(mod).__name__} detected. This task "
                f"restricts the design space to parallel-time architectures: "
                f"a sequential RNN simulates any finite automaton by "
                f"construction (Liu et al. 2023 Fig. 5 report a 1-layer LSTM "
                f"at 100% on every task), so it is the excluded skyline here."
            )


def _graph_depth(output: torch.Tensor) -> int:
    """Longest path length in the autograd graph rooted at `output`."""
    root = output.grad_fn
    if root is None:
        return 0
    depth: dict = {}
    stack = [root]
    while stack:
        node = stack[-1]
        if node in depth:
            stack.pop()
            continue
        pending = [
            child
            for child, _ in node.next_functions
            if child is not None and child not in depth
        ]
        if pending:
            stack.extend(pending)
        else:
            best = 0
            for child, _ in node.next_functions:
                if child is not None:
                    best = max(best, depth[child])
            depth[node] = 1 + best
            stack.pop()
    return depth[root]


def check_serial_depth(model: nn.Module, env_spec: EnvSpec,
                       config: TaskConfig, device: torch.device) -> None:
    """Reject architectures whose serial depth grows with sequence length.

    Two dummy batches (lengths depth_probe_short and depth_probe_long) are
    forwarded and the longest autograd paths compared. Constant-depth models
    (attention, convolutions) and log-depth associative scans pass; per-token
    python recurrences add thousands of serial nodes and fail.
    """
    was_training = model.training
    model.train()
    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
    depths = []
    for probe_len in (config.depth_probe_short, config.depth_probe_long):
        tokens = torch.randint(
            0, env_spec.alphabet_size, (2, probe_len),
            generator=gen, dtype=torch.long,
        ).to(device)
        logits = forward_logits(model, tokens, env_spec)
        depths.append(_graph_depth(logits))
    model.train(was_training)
    short_d, long_d = depths
    if long_d > short_d + config.depth_slack:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Serial-depth guard: autograd depth grew from {short_d} "
            f"(len {config.depth_probe_short}) to {long_d} "
            f"(len {config.depth_probe_long}); allowed slack is "
            f"{config.depth_slack}. Sequentially-recurrent computation is "
            f"not admissible in this task."
        )
    print(
        f"DEPTH_PROBE short={short_d} long={long_d} slack={config.depth_slack}",
        flush=True,
    )


@torch.no_grad()
def check_init_tripwire(model: nn.Module, env_spec: EnvSpec,
                        config: TaskConfig, device: torch.device) -> None:
    """Abort if the *untrained* model already simulates the automaton.

    Chance accuracy is at most 1/24; an untrained learned model sits near
    chance, while a hard-coded (or table-reading) simulator is near 1.0.
    """
    was_training = model.training
    model.eval()
    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(20240819)
    correct, total = 0, 0
    for _ in range(4):
        xb, yb = sample_batch(env_spec, config.batch_size, config.seq_len, gen)
        xb, yb = xb.to(device), yb.to(device)
        preds = forward_logits(model, xb, env_spec).argmax(dim=-1)
        correct += (preds == yb).sum().item()
        total += yb.numel()
    model.train(was_training)
    acc = correct / max(total, 1)
    print(f"INIT_TRIPWIRE acc={acc:.6f} threshold={config.init_tripwire_acc}",
          flush=True)
    if acc >= config.init_tripwire_acc:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Init tripwire: untrained model reaches accuracy {acc:.4f} "
            f">= {config.init_tripwire_acc} (chance <= 1/24). Hard-coding "
            f"the automaton instead of learning it is out of contract."
        )


# =====================================================================
# EDITABLE: model + optimizer + forward wrapper
# =====================================================================
class CustomSequenceModel(nn.Module):
    """NULL: position-wise MLP -- the logits at t depend only on x_t.

    No attention, no convolution, no scan, no recurrence: there is no path
    in this graph from position t' != t to the output at position t, so the
    model cannot track the automaton's state at all.  Width matches the
    reference Transformer (d_model = 512, MLP width 512) so the floor is
    architectural rather than a capacity handicap.
    """

    def __init__(self, vocab_size: int, num_states: int, max_len: int,
                 d_model: int = 512, hidden: int = 512):
        super().__init__()
        self.token_emb = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, d_model)
        self.mlp = nn.Sequential(
            nn.LayerNorm(d_model),
            nn.Linear(d_model, hidden),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Linear(hidden, d_model),
            nn.LayerNorm(d_model),
        )
        self.head = nn.Linear(d_model, num_states)

    def forward(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # [B, T] -> [B, T, d_model]; every position is processed on its own.
        x = self.token_emb(input_ids)
        x = x + self.mlp(x)
        return self.head(x)


def build_model(env_spec: EnvSpec, config: TaskConfig) -> nn.Module:
    """Construct the sequence model. Output: [B, T, num_states] logits."""
    return CustomSequenceModel(
        vocab_size=env_spec.alphabet_size,
        num_states=env_spec.num_states,
        max_len=env_spec.max_len,
        d_model=512,
        hidden=512,
    )


def get_optimizer_config(config: TaskConfig) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Same AdamW recipe as the reference baselines (Liu et al. 2023 App. B.3)."""
    return {"lr": 3e-4, "wd": 1e-4, "beta1": 0.9, "beta2": 0.999}


def forward_logits(model: nn.Module, input_ids: torch.Tensor,
                   env_spec: EnvSpec) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Run the model on `input_ids` and return logits [B, T, num_states]."""
    return model(input_ids)


# =====================================================================
# FIXED: training and evaluation driver
# =====================================================================
def evaluate(model: nn.Module, env_spec: EnvSpec, config: TaskConfig,
             device: torch.device, eval_seed: int) -> tuple[float, float]:
    model.eval()
    gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(eval_seed)
    correct, total, loss_sum = 0, 0, 0.0
    with torch.no_grad():
        for _ in range(config.eval_batches):
            xb, yb = sample_batch(env_spec, config.batch_size,
                                  config.seq_len, gen)
            xb = xb.to(device)
            yb = yb.to(device)
            logits = forward_logits(model, xb, env_spec)
            loss = F.cross_entropy(
                logits.reshape(-1, env_spec.num_states),
                yb.reshape(-1),
            )
            preds = logits.argmax(dim=-1)
            correct += (preds == yb).sum().item()
            total += yb.numel()
            loss_sum += loss.item() * yb.numel()
    return correct / max(total, 1), loss_sum / max(total, 1)


def train(env_spec: EnvSpec, config: TaskConfig,
          device: torch.device) -> dict[str, float]:
    set_global_seed(config.seed)
    # Editable code sees the public spec and a config with the automaton
    # seed masked: the transition table must be learned, not reconstructed.
    masked_config = replace(config, dfa_seed=-1)
    model = build_model(env_spec, masked_config).to(device)
    check_no_recurrent_modules(model)
    check_serial_depth(model, env_spec, config, device)
    check_init_tripwire(model, env_spec, config, device)
    opt_cfg = normalize_optimizer_config(get_optimizer_config(masked_config))
    optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(
        model.parameters(),
        lr=opt_cfg.lr, betas=(opt_cfg.beta1, opt_cfg.beta2),
        weight_decay=opt_cfg.wd,
    )
    n_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
    print(
        f"MODEL_CONFIG env={env_spec.name} alphabet={env_spec.alphabet_size} "
        f"states={env_spec.num_states} seq_len={env_spec.seq_len} "
        f"params={n_params}",
        flush=True,
    )
    print(
        f"OPT_CONFIG lr={opt_cfg.lr} wd={opt_cfg.wd} "
        f"beta1={opt_cfg.beta1} beta2={opt_cfg.beta2}",
        flush=True,
    )

    train_gen = torch.Generator().manual_seed(config.seed * 7919 + 1)
    stable_windows = 0
    last_train_acc = 0.0
    for step in range(1, config.train_steps + 1):
        model.train()
        xb, yb = sample_batch(env_spec, config.batch_size,
                              config.seq_len, train_gen)
        xb = xb.to(device)
        yb = yb.to(device)
        logits = forward_logits(model, xb, env_spec)
        loss = F.cross_entropy(
            logits.reshape(-1, env_spec.num_states),
            yb.reshape(-1),
        )
        optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        loss.backward()
        torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), config.max_grad_norm)
        optimizer.step()

        if step == 1 or step % config.log_interval == 0 or step == config.train_steps:
            train_acc = (logits.argmax(dim=-1) == yb).float().mean().item()
            last_train_acc = train_acc
            print(
                f"TRAIN_METRICS step={step} loss={loss.item():.6f} "
                f"train_acc={train_acc:.6f}",
                flush=True,
            )
            if train_acc >= config.early_stop_acc:
                stable_windows += 1
            else:
                stable_windows = 0
            if stable_windows >= config.early_stop_windows:
                print(f"EARLY_STOP step={step} train_acc={train_acc:.6f}",
                      flush=True)
                break

    eval_acc, eval_loss = evaluate(model, env_spec, config, device,
                                   eval_seed=config.seed * 100003 + 7)
    # Rescale so that chance level (1/|Q|) pins to 0.
    chance = 1.0 / env_spec.num_states
    score = max(0.0, (eval_acc - chance) / (1.0 - chance))
    return {
        "test_accuracy": eval_acc,
        "test_loss": eval_loss,
        "score": score,
        "last_train_acc": last_train_acc,
        "num_params": float(n_params),
    }


def resolve_device(arg: str) -> torch.device:
    if arg == "cpu":
        return torch.device("cpu")
    if arg == "cuda":
        if not torch.cuda.is_available():
            raise RuntimeError("CUDA requested but no GPU is available.")
        return torch.device("cuda")
    return torch.device("cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")


def maybe_apply_smoke(config: TaskConfig, enabled: bool) -> TaskConfig:
    if not enabled:
        return config
    return replace(
        config, train_steps=400, eval_batches=4, log_interval=100,
    )


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="MLS-Bench theory-semiautomata.")
    p.add_argument("--env", choices=tuple(_ENV_BUILDERS), default="s5_word")
    p.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    p.add_argument("--label", default="s5-word")
    p.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--device", choices=("auto", "cpu", "cuda"), default="auto")
    p.add_argument("--seq-len", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--train-steps", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--eval-batches", type=int, default=None)
    p.add_argument("--smoke", action="store_true")
    return p.parse_args()


def main() -> None:
    # The run script mints a per-run nonce and passes it here; the one scored
    # line carries it and the parser accepts exactly one line bearing it, so a
    # stray or forged `TEST_METRICS` print is not a score.
    import os as _os
    nonce = _os.environ.pop("MLSB_NONCE", "")
    args = parse_args()
    config = TaskConfig(env_name=args.env, seed=args.seed)
    if args.seq_len is not None:
        config = replace(config, seq_len=args.seq_len)
    if args.train_steps is not None:
        config = replace(config, train_steps=args.train_steps)
    if args.batch_size is not None:
        config = replace(config, batch_size=args.batch_size)
    if args.eval_batches is not None:
        config = replace(config, eval_batches=args.eval_batches)
    config = maybe_apply_smoke(config, args.smoke)

    device = resolve_device(args.device)
    env_spec = build_env_spec(config)
    print(
        "TASK_CONFIG "
        f"env={env_spec.name} alphabet={env_spec.alphabet_size} "
        f"states={env_spec.num_states} seq_len={env_spec.seq_len} "
        f"batch={config.batch_size} steps={config.train_steps} "
        f"eval_batches={config.eval_batches} seed={config.seed}",
        flush=True,
    )

    metrics = train(env_spec, config, device)
    print(
        "FINAL_METRICS "
        + " ".join(f"{k}={v:.6f}" for k, v in metrics.items()),
        flush=True,
    )
    print(
        f"TEST_METRICS[{nonce}] test_accuracy={metrics['test_accuracy']:.6f} "
        f"score={metrics['score']:.6f}",
        flush=True,
    )

    if args.output_dir is not None:
        args.output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        out = args.output_dir / f"{args.label}_seed{args.seed}.json"
        out.write_text(json.dumps({
            "config": asdict(config),
            "env": {
                "name": env_spec.name,
                "alphabet_size": env_spec.alphabet_size,
                "num_states": env_spec.num_states,
                "seq_len": env_spec.seq_len,
            },
            "metrics": metrics,
        }, indent=2))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
